Assert that events come in order

Source: R/events.R
ensure_sequence.Rd

A checkpoint for events that need another before them: an exam needs an enrolment, a move out a move in, a divorce a marriage. Every then event of a unit must come on or after the unit's first first event. The then events that come before it, or in a unit with no first event at all, are reported, with a reason column saying which. Returns data, so it can sit in the middle of a pipeline.

Usage

ensure_sequence(
  data,
  id,
  time,
  event,
  first,
  then,
  success_msg = NULL,
  warn_msg = NULL,
  abort_msg = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble, or a database or Arrow table: see Database and Arrow tables in checkpoints.

id

Column(s) identifying the unit (tidy-select), e.g. cpr.

time

The date or period of each event (one column).

event

The type of event (one column).

first

The event that must come first, e.g. "enrolled".

then

The event that must not come before it, e.g. "exam".

success_msg

Message shown when the rule holds. If NULL (default), it is "Check passed: <message>" when warn_msg or abort_msg is given, so the console names every check that ran, and a description of the check otherwise.

warn_msg

Message shown when events come out of order and no abort_msg is set. Defaults to a description of the check.

abort_msg

If provided, cli::cli_abort() is called with this message when the rule is broken. If NULL (default), a warning is issued instead.

Value

data invisibly, unchanged.

Details

Events on the same day are in order. Rows with a missing time are only reported when the unit has no first event. The unit is what the id columns say: give id = c(cpr, education) when an exam needs an enrolment in the same education.

Too many events of one kind, such as two deaths, is ensure_counts() with the event as the role.

See also

describe_events(), ensure_transitions() for a status that changes over time, checkpoints.

Examples

events <- data.frame(
  cpr   = c("a", "a", "b", "b", "c"),
  date  = as.Date(c("2020-08-15", "2021-06-01", "2021-06-01", "2021-08-15",
                    "2021-06-01")),
  event = c("enrolled", "exam", "exam", "enrolled", "exam")
)
# b takes an exam before enrolling, c without enrolling
ensure_sequence(events, cpr, date, event, first = "enrolled", then = "exam")
#> Warning: exam before enrolled per cpr
#> ℹ 2 rows in 2 groups
#>   In 2 units
#>   Reasons: before enrolled (1), no enrolled (1)
#> ℹ The rows:
#>     reason          cpr   date       event
#>     <chr>           <chr> <date>     <chr>
#>   1 before enrolled b     2021-06-01 exam
#>   2 no enrolled     c     2021-06-01 exam
